snippets.title: Snippets
snippets.name: Name
snippets.adhocHint: Runs once on every host you tick, and shows each one's output. Not saved; for a command you use again, make a snippet.
help.historyMin: A command you typed is suggested again once you used it this often, or right after you used it (within the hour). One used once and not again in 30 days is forgotten.
help.memoryMode: This session lives in Burrow's memory, not in tmux on the host: chosen for this session, set for the host, or the host has no tmux. It keeps running when you close the tab and several devices can use it, but a restart or update of Burrow ends it. To keep sessions across restarts, start them in tmux (New session, or the host's tmux setting); a host without tmux needs it installed first (e.g. sudo apt install tmux). A tmux you start in it yourself keeps running on the host: tmux attach in a new session brings it back.
help.aiOwnNetwork: Log lines sent to the model have their IP addresses masked, unless you tick this. Tick it only when this server runs on a machine you control on your own network: a name like "gpu" or an address over a VPN can just as well be a rented machine elsewhere. Secrets, keys, tokens and e-mail addresses are masked either way.
help.aiTimeout: How long a local model may take for one analysis, from the question to the last word. A small model on a small machine may need minutes before the first word; a Claude analysis is not limited by this.
help.aiPrices: What your provider charges per million tokens, read and written. With these Burrow shows an estimate beside each answer; without them only the tokens. Local models cost nothing here.
help.sessions: A session keeps running when you close the tab or lock the phone. Open it again from any device to see the same screen. Only "Close session" or typing exit ends it.
help.snippets: Saved commands. Run one in the terminal with the lightning button, or here on several hosts at once with the output per host.
help.snippetSuggestions: Commands typed at least three times in Burrow's terminals, on all hosts together. What is quicker to type (one word, cd, ls) is left out. Hiding one keeps it in the history for completion.
help.snippetVariables: Write {{name}} for a value you fill in each time, e.g. docker logs {{container}} (it offers the running containers). {{name=value}} starts with a value, {{name=a|b|c}} gives a choice, {{name=}} may stay empty.
help.snippetScope: Where the snippet shows up in the terminal: on every host, on the hosts of one group (and its subgroups), or on one host.
help.hostGroup: A host inherits user, port, key and other settings from its group and the groups above it. Anything you set here overrides that.
help.hostAuth: Key: log in with a key from the vault (recommended). Password: log in with the stored password. Inherit: what the group says; automatic when nothing above says: the key if one is chosen, else the stored password.
help.hostPassword: Stored encrypted. Also used by the key button in the terminal to type it at a sudo prompt.
help.hostTags: Labels for searching, e.g. docker, pi, backup. Search matches them too.
help.hostStartup: Typed once when a new session starts, e.g. cd /data. Not repeated when you reopen a session.
help.hostTmux: With tmux the session survives a restart of Burrow. "Use when available" picks tmux if the host has it and falls back to a session in Burrow's memory. Burrow runs its own tmux server (tmux -L burrow), so your own tmux setup is not touched.
help.hostTerm: The terminal type announced to the host. Leave empty for xterm-256color, which suits almost everything.
help.hostEncoding: Character set of the host's output. Leave empty for UTF-8.
help.groupDefaults: Hosts in this group, and in groups inside it, use these values unless they set their own.
help.push: Burrow's own notifications, straight to this browser or the Android app. Which ones is set per channel: Settings -> Notification channels -> Burrow's own push. In the app they need a UnifiedPush app on the phone to carry them, such as the ntfy app; each message is encrypted for this device, so that app cannot read it.
help.allHosts: The top of the chain: a host's own value first, then its group and the groups above it, then these, then Burrow's own defaults (port 22, tmux when available). The host's form says where an empty field's value comes from.
help.keyVault: Generate a key here and install it on a host with "Install key on host". Imported keys may have a passphrase; it is stored encrypted too.
help.passkeys: A passkey signs you in with your fingerprint, face or screen lock. Add one per device you use.
help.password: Optional. A password only works together with the authenticator app.
help.totp: Six-digit codes from an app such as Aegis or Google Authenticator. Needed for password sign-in, and usable to confirm sensitive actions.
help.recovery: Each code signs you in once when you lose your passkey or phone. Keep them offline.
help.devices: Every browser signed in to your account. Signing one out ends its connection immediately; its terminal sessions keep running.
help.knownHosts: Host keys you trusted. If a host is reinstalled its key changes and Burrow refuses to connect; delete the old entry here and connect again.
help.theme: Auto follows the light or dark setting of your device. Stored per device.
help.keyBar: Keys separated by spaces. Names: esc tab enter bs del ins space up down left right home end pgup pgdn f1...f12. Combine with + and ctrl, alt or shift: shift+tab, ctrl+c, alt+bs, ctrl+left. Plain ctrl and alt stick until the next key. Anything else is typed as is (e.g. | ~ /). Stored per device.

help.updateWindow: When the window opens (every day, one day a week, or by a cron expression) Burrow checks every Docker host for image updates, tells you about new ones through your channels (topic "updates"), and updates the stacks that opted in. help.smart: SMART is what a disk says about its own health. Burrow reads it with smartctl every six hours: install smartmontools on the host (apt install smartmontools) and store the host's password in Burrow (sudo asks for it), or let the SSH user run smartctl without one: a sudoers line such as  youruser ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/sbin/smartctl. Burrow judges each disk by the five counts Backblaze found to go with failing disks (SMART 5, 187, 188, 197, 198): any above zero is worth watching; growing since the oldest check kept (one a day, 90 days) means failing, except command timeouts (188), which are often a cable and stay at watching. A disk that fails, gets new bad sectors or wears out raises an alert.

help.diskIo: Each whole disk's reads and writes per second, and how much of the time it was busy (iostat's %util), over the same second as the CPU. A hard disk that is busy a little all day never gets to spin down. Open a disk for its history and, as an admin, which processes read and write.
disk.noHistory: No history for this disk yet: Burrow keeps its counters with every five-minute sample.
help.diskWho: While this is open, Burrow reads every process's I/O counters (/proc/<pid>/io) twice, two seconds apart, every few seconds: no agent, no iotop, and nothing keeps running when you close it. As root (through sudo with the host's stored password, or sudo without one) it sees every process; otherwise only the SSH user's own. A process's counters are for all disks together: the files it has open tell which disk it uses. A write is counted when it is made; the kernel puts it on the disk later, so a disk can be busy with no process seen.
disk.adminOnly: Which processes use this disk: for admins (it reads every process as root).
disk.sampled: Measured over {s} s at {at}; again every few seconds while this is open.
disk.asUser: Only the SSH user's own processes: {seen} of {total} could be read. As root Burrow would see them all: store the host's password in Burrow, or allow sudo without one.
disk.partial: {seen} of {total} processes could be read: the others ended meanwhile, or not even root may read them (a container without CAP_SYS_PTRACE).
disk.proc.unread: Its open files could not be read (it ended, or it is not allowed).
disk.proc.noFiles: No files open: what it read or wrote is closed already.
disk.nobodyHere: No process with a file on {name} read or wrote in these seconds.
disk.unexplained: {name} moved {w} in these seconds without a process seen with a file on it: the kernel writing out earlier writes, the filesystem's journal, or a file closed already.

disk.noContainers: No container read or wrote on {name} in these seconds.
disk.totals: Rates are per process, all disks together (/proc/<pid>/io). W: a file open for writing, R: for reading.
